blocks.prompt: 9 Given the function \(f(x) = \ln x\). Find the equation of the transformed function after applying in order, the vertical stretch by factor 4, shift 6 units to right, horizontal compress by factor 3, and shift 1 unit upward. Draw the graphs of both the original and transformed functions on the same coordinate plane.
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal ke do hisse hain: pehle chaar transformations se naya function, phir dono graphs.
Diya kya hai? \(f(x) = \ln x\).
Find kya karna hai? Naya function g, aur f aur g ke graphs ek hi plane par.
Rule: 4 se stretch = 4 se zarb; 6 daayen = \(x \to x - 6\); 3 se compression = \(x \to 3x\); 1 oopar = 1 jama.
Plan: tarteeb se qadam, phir asymptote ka safar dekh kar graph.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = \ln x\), \(x > 0\).
Maloom karna: transformed function \(g\), aur \(f\) aur \(g\) ka graph saath saath.
Tareeqa: \(y = 4f(x)\); \(y = g(x - 6)\); \(y = g(3x)\); phir 1 jama. Har qadam sab se naye function par.

Qadam 1: 4 se vertical stretch
\[g_{1}(x) = 4\ln x\]
Kyun: \(a = 4\) har output ko chaar guna karta hai.

Qadam 2: 6 units daayen
\[g_{2}(x) = 4\ln(x - 6)\]
Kyun: \(g_{1}\) ke har \(x\) ki jagah \(x - 6\); bahar wala 4 waisa hi raha.

Qadam 3: 3 se horizontal compression
\[g_{3}(x) = 4\ln(3x - 6)\]
Kyun: \(g_{2}\) ke har \(x\) ki jagah \(3x\): \(x - 6\) ban gaya \(3x - 6\).
Dhyan dein: \(3(x - 6) = 3x - 18\) ghalat hai; sirf \(x\) ko \(3x\) banana hai, 6 ko nahin chhoona.

Qadam 4: 1 unit oopar
\[g(x) = 4\ln(3x - 6) + 1\]
Kyun: oopar 1 ke liye har output mein 1 jama.

g ke graph ki khaas baatein
\[3x - 6 > 0 \Rightarrow x > 2\]
\[g\left(\tfrac{7}{3}\right) = 4\ln 1 + 1 = 1\]
\[g(3) = 4\ln 3 + 1 \approx 5.39\]
\[g(4) = 4\ln 6 + 1 \approx 8.17\]
\[x\text{-intercept}: x = 2 + \tfrac{1}{3}e^{-1/4} \approx 2.26\]
Kyun: \(\ln x\) ka asymptote \(x = 0\) pehle 6 daayen ho kar \(x = 6\) bana, phir 3 se compression mein \(x = \frac{6}{3} = 2\). \(x\)-intercept ke liye \(g = 0\): \(\ln(3x - 6) = -\frac{1}{4}\), yani \(3x - 6 = e^{-1/4}\). \(\frac{7}{3}\) is liye chuna ke \(3x - 6 = 1\) ho aur \(\ln 1 = 0\) aasaan ho.

Dono graphs banaiye
\(f(x) = \ln x\): asymptote \(x = 0\) (\(y\)-axis), \((1, 0)\) aur \((e, 1)\) se guzarta hai. \(g\): asymptote \(x = 2\), points \(\left(\frac{7}{3}, 1\right)\), \((3, 5.39)\), \((4, 8.17)\); yeh \(\ln x\) se chaar guna tez chadhta hai.
Kyun: points aur asymptote mil kar curve ki jagah pakki kar dete hain. Pehle dashed asymptote kheenchiye, phir points, phir smooth curve.

Tasdeeq:
\(\ln x\) ka point \((1, 0)\) follow karein: stretch \(\to (1, 0)\); 6 daayen \(\to (7, 0)\); 3 se compression \(\to \left(\frac{7}{3}, 0\right)\); 1 oopar \(\to \left(\frac{7}{3}, 1\right)\). Aur waqai \(g\left(\frac{7}{3}\right) = 1\).
blocks.final_answer: \(g(x) = 4\ln(3x - 6) + 1\), \(x > 2\); is ka asymptote \(x = 2\) hai aur yeh \(\left(\frac{7}{3}, 1\right)\) se guzarta hai; figure mein \(f(x) = \ln x\) ke saath bana hai.

answer_figure.alt: The curve f(x) = ln x through (1, 0) with the y-axis as asymptote, and the curve g(x) = 4 ln(3x - 6) + 1 rising steeply from the dashed asymptote x = 2 through (7/3, 1), (3, 5.39) and (4, 8.17).
answer_figure.caption: f(x) = ln x and g(x) = 4 ln(3x − 6) + 1
